checks.explanation: The claim is a verbatim quote from the source document describing an art installation where the student programmed a microcontroller and tuned thresholds. The attribution 'student' matches the first-person 'I' in the text.

The label 'shared' implies collaborative work, but the source text only states 'For an art installation, I programmed...'. While 'art installation' often implies a team, the text does not explicitly describe collaboration or shared ownership. The rationale assumes a collaborative environment without explicit evidence in the quote. Without explicit mention of teammates or shared tasks, individual contribution ('student') is more accurate than 'shared'.

The student describes specific design choices: varying LED patterns based on sensor inputs and tuning thresholds to constraints (sensor readings). This goes beyond simple application; it involves adapting methods to specific artistic/functional constraints, fitting the 'designed' label.
The phrase 'tuned thresholds during gallery tests' explicitly states a concrete test method used for evaluation. This supports the 'described' label for evaluation.

The text implies a successful outcome ('vary LED patterns', 'tuned thresholds') which constitutes a reported concrete outcome. No quantitative metric or external adoption is stated, so 'reported' is appropriate.
Programming requires an explicit programming action and artifact; comparison, deployment, measurement, or tool context alone is not enough.

The activity involves integrating digital logic (microcontroller code) with sensors (proximity-sensor) and actuators (LED patterns) within a physical hardware system. This fits the definition of designing or integrating components within an embedded hardware system.
The source text explicitly names 'microcontroller' as the tool used for programming.

dimensions.description: Individual contribution explicitly described in the evidence.

labels.assisted: Explicitly supported another contributor or followed guided work.
labels.shared: Explicit individual contribution within collaborative work.
labels.led: Explicitly directed the work or independently owned the deliverable; a title or possessive like my thesis alone is insufficient.

dimensions.description: Nature of the work demonstrated by the description, not prestige.

labels.unknown: A title, skill list, or credential alone does not describe the work.
labels.applied: Used established methods to implement or complete a described task.
labels.designed: Made and explained design choices or adapted methods to constraints.
labels.investigated: Investigated a question through an explicit method and analysis.

dimensions.description: How the work was evaluated; no implied ordering across disciplines.

labels.described: A concrete test, review, or assessment method is stated.
labels.compared: Evaluation includes explicit baselines, alternatives, or controls.
labels.externally_reviewed: External assessment is explicitly stated; this remains a claim until verified.

dimensions.description: Evidence describing results, separate from their independent verification.

labels.reported: A concrete outcome is reported without a measurement method.
labels.measured: An outcome and measurement method or comparison are stated.
labels.adopted: Actual use or adoption by identified users or an organization is stated.

category_guidance.project: Distinguish guided replication from individual design. Tool names do not establish depth. Preserve team contribution and ask about missing evaluation.
category_guidance.work: Assess described responsibilities and contributions. Employer reputation and job title do not establish ownership. Do not sum overlapping durations.
category_guidance.research: Unpublished research can demonstrate investigation. Evaluate methods and contribution independently of publication status; do not invent publications.
category_guidance.publication: Separate paper content, authorship, and review status. Do not rank unfamiliar venues or assume arXiv entails peer review. Request metadata verification later.
category_guidance.coursework: Preserve course and grade context. Enrollment alone does not establish mastery or independent implementation.
category_guidance.education: Preserve every degree and original grade scale separately. No prestige adjustment or invented grade conversion. Do not infer completion from attendance dates.
category_guidance.activity: Assess individual contribution in community, creative, leadership, and school activities without requiring technical work or publications.
category_guidance.other: Preserve unfamiliar evidence and uncertainty. Do not force it into a known technical competency or discard it because of taxonomy coverage.
